sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取nytimes.com/subscribe上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯，这是周日版的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today we've got a little something different for you because our colleagues over at Serial Productions have a new series out that we're excited to share.
sentences.zh: 今天我们为您准备了一些特别的内容，因为我们的Serial Productions同事发布了一个新系列，我们很高兴能与大家分享。

sentences.en: It's called The Last 12 Weeks, and it follows a team of death penalty lawyers in their last-minute scramble to try to stop their client's execution in Texas.
sentences.zh: 它叫《最后12周》，讲述了一支死刑辩护律师团队在德克萨斯州为阻止客户被处决而进行的最后冲刺。

sentences.en: And what's kind of incredible about it is that the team at Serial managed to convince a team of death penalty lawyers
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，Serial团队竟然说服了一支死刑辩护律师团队，

sentences.en: to let them follow them around in the middle of an actual case.
sentences.zh: 让他们在实际案件审理过程中全程跟拍。

sentences.en: They put microphones in the room as the lawyers tried to argue their case to witnesses, to the media, to a victim's mother.
sentences.zh: 当律师们试图向证人、媒体和受害者母亲辩护时，他们把麦克风放进了房间里。

sentences.en: And these are the kinds of behind-the-scenes conversations you rarely get to hear, and they are riveting.
sentences.zh: 这些都是你难得一见的幕后对话，非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: And so we're sharing the first episode of the five-part series, a collaboration with The Marshall Project and hosted by reporter Maurice Chamas.
sentences.zh: 所以我们分享了这个五集系列的第一集，这是与The Marshall Project的合作项目，由记者莫里斯·查马斯主持。

sentences.en: You can find all episodes by searching for The Last 12 Weeks wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您可以在任何收听播客的地方搜索《最后12周》来找到所有剧集。

sentences.en: Okay, here's the show.
sentences.zh: 好了，节目开始。

sentences.en: In the fall of 2024, a criminal defense lawyer got the kind of phone call that most lawyers can only dream about.
sentences.zh: 2024年秋天，一位刑事辩护律师接到了大多数律师梦寐以求的那种电话。

sentences.en: It concerned a client of his, a guy named David Wood, one of Texas' most notorious serial killers.
sentences.zh: 电话是关于他的客户，一个叫大卫·伍德的人，他是德克萨斯州最臭名昭著的连环杀手之一。

sentences.en: He was sitting on death row, months away from his execution.
sentences.zh: 他当时身处死囚牢房，距离被处决仅剩几个月。

sentences.en: The man on the phone, George Hall, thought something corrupt had gone down in David Wood's trial.
sentences.zh: 电话那头的人叫乔治·霍尔，他认为大卫·伍德的审判中存在腐败行为。

sentences.en: It had happened more than 30 years ago, but for 30 years he'd said nothing, mostly because he was afraid to.
sentences.zh: 那件事发生在30多年前，但他30年来一直没敢说，主要是因为害怕。

sentences.en: For those 30 years, he'd been on parole.
sentences.zh: 在那30年里，他一直处于假释期。

sentences.en: He worried if he aggravated the authorities, they might find some way to send him back to prison.
sentences.zh: 他担心如果激怒了当局，他们可能会想方设法把他送回监狱。

sentences.en: But now his parole had ended, and George Hall was ready to tell his story, which he'd eventually put into a sworn declaration.
sentences.zh: 但现在他的假释期结束了，乔治·霍尔准备讲述他的故事，并最终将其写成了宣誓书。

sentences.en: That story goes like this.
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的。

sentences.en: Back in the late 80s,
sentences.zh: 回到80年代末，

sentences.en: George Hall and David Wood were locked up together at the Easton Unit in Texas.
sentences.zh: 乔治·霍尔和大卫·伍德一起被关在德克萨斯州的伊斯顿监狱。

sentences.en: George Hall was in for murder.
sentences.zh: 乔治·霍尔是因为谋杀入狱。

sentences.en: David Wood was in for rape.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德是因为强奸入狱。

sentences.en: They weren't particularly close.
sentences.zh: 他们关系并不特别亲近。

sentences.en: David Wood was quiet, didn't talk much.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德很安静，话不多。

sentences.en: But when he did, George says, it was mainly to complain about how the police in his hometown of El Paso were harassing him, investigating him for a series of murders.
sentences.zh: 但乔治说，当他开口时，主要是抱怨他家乡埃尔帕索的警察如何骚扰他，调查他涉及的一系列谋杀案。

sentences.en: Basically what he said was
sentences.zh: 基本上他所说的是，

sentences.en: El Paso was trying to pin it on him.
sentences.zh: 埃尔帕索警方试图把罪名扣在他头上。

sentences.en: David Wood insisted he had nothing to do with those murders.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德坚称他与那些谋杀案毫无关系。

sentences.en: George thought maybe he didn't, maybe he did.
sentences.zh: 乔治心想也许他没做，也许做了。

sentences.en: Either way, he didn't really care.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他并不在乎。

sentences.en: Eventually, George and David Wood were separated, moved to different facilities hundreds of miles apart.
sentences.zh: 最终，乔治和大卫·伍德被分开了，转移到了相隔数百英里的不同设施。

sentences.en: One day, George says he's in the prison library, ready to go to lunch, when two officers come in and tell him to pack his stuff.
sentences.zh: 有一天，乔治说他正在监狱图书馆准备去吃午饭，两名警官进来让他收拾东西。

sentences.en: I said, well, where am I going?
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我要去哪儿？

sentences.en: They wouldn't tell me.
sentences.zh: 他们不肯告诉我。

sentences.en: So, next thing I know,
sentences.zh: 所以，接下来我知道的是，

sentences.en: I'm on a bus ride down to El Paso.
sentences.zh: 我坐上了去埃尔帕索的巴士。

sentences.en: A few hours later,
sentences.zh: 几个小时后，

sentences.en: George finds himself in a holding cell in the El Paso County Jail.
sentences.zh: 乔治发现自己被关在埃尔帕索县监狱的拘留室里。

sentences.en: Two other guys join him in there.
sentences.zh: 另外两个人也进来了。

sentences.en: George recognizes them both as guys who had celled with David Wood.
sentences.zh: 乔治认出他们俩都曾和大卫·伍德关在一起。

sentences.en: And one of them says to the group, they have an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人对大家说，他们有一个机会。

sentences.en: They can all get money, maybe, or less prison time.
sentences.zh: 他们可能都能拿到钱，或者减刑。

sentences.en: All they have to do is snitch on David Wood.
sentences.zh: 他们要做的就是举报大卫·伍德。

sentences.en: Soon enough, they're escorted out of the cell and into a car.
sentences.zh: 很快，他们被带出牢房，坐进了一辆车。

sentences.en: And George says, that's when the cops start rolling out the red carpet.
sentences.zh: 乔治说，就在那时，警察开始铺红地毯了。

sentences.en: They give us the tour of scenic drive up the mountainside, look across the Rio Grande, look into old Mexico and this and that.
sentences.zh: 他们带我们游览了山腰的风景大道，眺望格兰德河，看向老墨西哥等等。

sentences.en: Whatever, you know.
sentences.zh: 随便吧，你知道的。

sentences.en: And I'm sitting there thinking to myself, we're not handcuffed.
sentences.zh: 我坐在那儿心想，我们没戴手铐。

sentences.en: What if we jump out and run?
sentences.zh: 如果我们跳车逃跑会怎样？

sentences.en: What are they going to do then, you know?
sentences.zh: 他们能拿我们怎么办，你知道吗？

sentences.en: But he sits tight.
sentences.zh: 但他还是按兵不动。

sentences.en: George says they're taken to a hamburger joint for lunch and then, ultimately, to a police station.
sentences.zh: 乔治说他们被带到一家汉堡店吃午饭，最后被带到了警察局。

sentences.en: The guys are offered coffee, snacks, cigarettes, and then they're ushered into a room with detectives.
sentences.zh: 这些人被提供了咖啡、零食、香烟，然后被带进了一个有侦探的房间。

sentences.en: Of course, they got files everywhere.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们到处都是档案。

sentences.en: They got David Wood's name pastored, all over the thing.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德的名字贴满了整个地方。

sentences.en: They got arrows and lines going to this, this, dates wrote down.
sentences.zh: 他们画了箭头和线条指向这里那里，写下了日期。

sentences.en: Files are sitting there.
sentences.zh: 档案就放在那儿。

sentences.en: They've started handing us files.
sentences.zh: 他们开始把档案递给我们。

sentences.en: Look at this.
sentences.zh: 看看这个。

sentences.en: We got this on him.
sentences.zh: 我们掌握了他这个证据。

sentences.en: We got this on him.
sentences.zh: 我们掌握了他那个证据。

sentences.en: He did this.
sentences.zh: 他做了这个。

sentences.en: We know this, this, this, this.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这个、这个、这个、这个。

sentences.en: And going through all facts and stuff, this narrative-driven shit, and you're reading what they got.
sentences.zh: 翻看所有的事实和资料，这些叙事驱动的鬼话，你读着他们掌握的东西。

sentences.en: And then they, after that, they go, you know anything?
sentences.zh: 然后在那之后，他们问，你知道什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, I don't know a goddamn thing.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我他妈什么都不知道。

sentences.en: All they had to do was ask me at the prison unit.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以在监狱里直接问我。

sentences.en: I was maddered and shit about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: As for the other two guys.
sentences.zh: 至于另外两个人。

sentences.en: They go back.
sentences.zh: 他们回去了。

sentences.en: They're talking to each other, but it's in real low tone.
sentences.zh: 他们互相交谈，但声音压得很低。

sentences.en: And they basically don't even want to talk to me about nothing.
sentences.zh: 基本上他们甚至不想跟我谈任何事。

sentences.en: So I knew to myself right then and there,
sentences.zh: 所以我当时就对自己说，

sentences.en: they're going to say whatever they want them to say.
sentences.zh: 他们会说任何警察想让他们说的话。

sentences.en: They're going to tell the police that David Wood confessed to multiple murders.
sentences.zh: 他们会告诉警察大卫·伍德承认了多起谋杀案。

sentences.en: But George is sure these guys don't actually know anything about David Wood.
sentences.zh: 但乔治确信这些人根本不知道关于大卫·伍德的任何事情。

sentences.en: He would have heard about it already.
sentences.zh: 如果知道，他早就听说了。

sentences.en: Plus, he knows they're not above lying.
sentences.zh: 而且，他知道这些人撒谎成性。

sentences.en: George returns to prison.
sentences.zh: 乔治回到了监狱。

sentences.en: Not long after, he writes to an El Paso prosecutor about, quote,
sentences.zh: 不久之后，他写信给埃尔帕索的一位检察官，提到，引用：

sentences.en: improprieties that I am aware of.
sentences.zh: “我所知道的不正当行为”。

sentences.en: He says he knows the informants are fabricating their stories.
sentences.zh: 他说他知道那些线人是在编造故事。

sentences.en: The prosecutor never writes back, but the letter does make its way into David Wood's case file.
sentences.zh: 检察官从未回信，但那封信确实进入了大卫·伍德的案卷。

sentences.en: Eventually, David Wood does go on trial for the murders.
sentences.zh: 最终，大卫·伍德确实因谋杀案受审。

sentences.en: George is never called to testify.
sentences.zh: 乔治从未被传唤作证。

sentences.en: But the two other guys become the star witnesses for the prosecution.
sentences.zh: 但另外两个人成了控方的明星证人。

sentences.en: The jury convicts David Wood, and he's sentenced to death.
sentences.zh: 陪审团判定大卫·伍德有罪，他被判处死刑。

sentences.en: Court documents show that after the trial, one of the informants received $13,000 in reward money.
sentences.zh: 法庭文件显示，审判后，其中一名线人获得了13,000美元的奖金。

sentences.en: The other got his own capital murder charge dropped.
sentences.zh: 另一人则撤销了他自己的谋杀重罪指控。

sentences.en: I identified more than a dozen officers, detectives, and supervisors who were involved in David Wood's case.
sentences.zh: 我确定了十几名参与大卫·伍德案件的警官、侦探和主管。

sentences.en: I wanted to ask them about George Hall.
sentences.zh: 我想问他们关于乔治·霍尔的事。

sentences.en: Some were dead, one had dementia, one hung up on me, and others never responded.
sentences.zh: 有些人已经去世，一个患有痴呆症，一个挂断了我的电话，其他人从未回应。

sentences.en: But the one detective who did speak to me extensively about the case called George's whole story, quote, preposterous.
sentences.zh: 但唯一一位与我深入探讨此案的侦探称乔治的整个故事是，引用，“荒谬绝伦”。

sentences.en: It's pretty well documented in court records and a media account that George and the other two men were brought in together and interviewed by the El Paso police.
sentences.zh: 法庭记录和媒体报道中都有充分记录，乔治和其他两人是被一起带走并由埃尔帕索警方审讯的。

sentences.en: But the detective said he couldn't imagine his colleagues taking prisoners out for a joyride and showing them case materials in order to get them to snitch.
sentences.zh: 但那位侦探说，他无法想象他的同事会带囚犯出去兜风并展示案卷材料来诱导他们举报。

sentences.en: For more than 30 years after David Wood's trial,
sentences.zh: 在大卫·伍德审判后的30多年里，

sentences.en: George kept tabs on the case, googled it from time to time.
sentences.zh: 乔治一直关注着这个案子，时不时地谷歌搜索一下。

sentences.en: In 2009, he read that David Wood's execution was called off.
sentences.zh: 2009年，他读到大卫·伍德的处决被叫停了。

sentences.en: There'd been a question about his intellectual capacity.
sentences.zh: 当时对他是否有智力障碍存在疑问。

sentences.en: But by 2024,
sentences.zh: 但到了2024年，

sentences.en: George saw that David Wood was again scheduled for execution.
sentences.zh: 乔治看到大卫·伍德再次被安排处决。

sentences.en: This time, George figured it would actually happen.
sentences.zh: 这一次，乔治觉得这真的会发生。

sentences.en: And this time, he was finally off parole.
sentences.zh: 而且这一次，他终于结束了假释。

sentences.en: So if he was going to speak up, it was now or never.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他要说出来，现在就是最后的机会。

sentences.en: I don't know if it's going to make a difference whether he gets executed or not.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他是否会被处决，这会有什么不同。

sentences.en: That's not the question.
sentences.zh: 那不是问题所在。

sentences.en: That's not what I got to live with.
sentences.zh: 那不是我必须面对的生活。

sentences.en: What I have to live with is,
sentences.zh: 我必须面对的是，

sentences.en: can I live with myself
sentences.zh: 我能否问心无愧地活着，

sentences.en: knowing that I know two people
sentences.zh: 明知我有两个认识的人

sentences.en: fabricated testimony to get a guy executed
sentences.zh: 编造了证词来让一个人被处决，

sentences.en: and I don't say anything about it.
sentences.zh: 而我却对此只字不提。

sentences.en: Not long after George Hall called David Wood's lawyer,
sentences.zh: 在乔治·霍尔给大卫·伍德的律师打电话后不久，

sentences.en: David Wood's lawyer emailed me asking me to write about the case.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德的律师给我发了电子邮件，请我写写这个案子。

sentences.en: I wasn't surprised.
sentences.zh: 我并不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: I'm a journalist at a non-profit called The Marshall Project where we cover the criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 我是非营利组织The Marshall Project的记者，我们负责报道刑事司法系统。

sentences.en: I'm the death penalty guy on staff, as gloomy as that sounds.
sentences.zh: 我是员工里的死刑专家，听起来很阴郁。

sentences.en: But I was surprised by who was asking.
sentences.zh: 但我对提出请求的人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Greg Warchuk.
sentences.zh: 格雷格·瓦尔丘克。

sentences.en: I know Greg Warchuk as a big deal in capital defense work.
sentences.zh: 我知道格雷格·瓦尔丘克在死刑辩护领域是个大人物。

sentences.en: He's been defending people on death row for decades and even stopped one execution by winning at the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 他几十年来一直为死囚辩护，甚至通过在最高法院胜诉阻止了一次处决。

sentences.en: I'd asked him for an interview years ago for a book I was writing on the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 多年前我曾为我写的一本关于死刑的书向他申请采访。

sentences.en: He said no.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝了。

sentences.en: He rarely spoke to reporters.
sentences.zh: 他很少接受记者采访。

sentences.en: But now here he was in my inbox.
sentences.zh: 但现在他出现在我的收件箱里。

sentences.en: His email was polite and panicky.
sentences.zh: 他的邮件礼貌而惊慌。

sentences.en: David Wood's execution date was only 17 weeks away.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德的处决日期只剩下17周了。

sentences.en: He wanted me to write about the case and all the problems he saw with it.
sentences.zh: 他希望我写写这个案子以及他所看到的所有问题。

sentences.en: I was pretty skeptical.
sentences.zh: 我当时相当怀疑。

sentences.en: I did the hard-hitting research of reading the Wikipedia page about David Wood and, woof, six women and girls, one as young as 14, killed and buried in the desert
sentences.zh: 我做了深入的研究，阅读了关于大卫·伍德的维基百科页面，天哪，六名妇女和女孩，最小的才14岁，被杀害并埋在沙漠里，

sentences.en: outside of El Paso.
sentences.zh: 在埃尔帕索郊外。

sentences.en: David Wood even got one of those spooky serial killer nicknames, the Desert Killer.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德甚至得到了一个令人毛骨悚然的连环杀手绰号，“沙漠杀手”。

sentences.en: Greg wrote to me that David Wood was innocent, that he didn't commit any of these murders.
sentences.zh: 格雷格写信告诉我大卫·伍德是无辜的，他没有犯下任何这些谋杀案。

sentences.en: And sure, I did find George Hall's story compelling, but even if those informants were lying at the trial, that doesn't mean
sentences.zh: 当然，我确实觉得乔治·霍尔的故事很引人注目，但即使那些线人在审判中撒谎，也不意味着

sentences.en: David Wood didn't do it.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德没做过这些事。

sentences.en: Plus, in order to do the story
sentences.zh: 另外，为了完成这个报道，

sentences.en: Greg was pitching,
sentences.zh: 格雷格（Greg）当时正在推销这个案子，

sentences.en: I'd have to reinvestigate it from scratch, all six murders in a matter of weeks.
sentences.zh: 我得从头开始重新调查，在几周内查清全部六起谋杀案。

sentences.zh: 与此同时，

sentences.en: So yeah, this is the case that Greg Warchuk is trying to fight.
sentences.zh: 所以没错，这就是格雷格·沃丘克试图抗争的案件。

sentences.en: A hideous case in which the jury needed less than 90 minutes to hand down
sentences.zh: 一个令人发指的案件，陪审团仅用了不到90分钟就做出了裁决，

sentences.en: over the course of three decades, numerous appeals courts have found no reason to question.
sentences.zh: 在过去三十年里，无数上诉法院都认为没有理由质疑这一裁决。

sentences.en: But Greg is adamant that the cops, the prosecutors, the jury, the judges, they all got it wrong.

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Greg is a law professor at the University of Wisconsin in Madison, where he just flew in from.
sentences.zh: 格雷格是威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校的法学教授，他刚从那里飞过来。

sentences.en: There's a nervous energy wafting off of him.
sentences.zh: 他身上散发着一种紧张不安的气息。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, should I start from the top?
sentences.zh: 是啊，我是说，我应该从头说起吗？

sentences.en: Can we just start with what's important to you right now?
sentences.zh: 我们能直接从你现在最关心的事情开始吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, what's important to me right now is I'm hoping to see the incoming district attorney of El Paso who was elected in November.
sentences.zh: 好的，我现在最关心的是，我希望能见到11月刚当选的埃尔帕索候任地方检察官。

sentences.en: Greg took on David Wood as a client back in 2009, the first time
sentences.zh: 格雷格是在2009年接手大卫·伍德案的，那是第一次

sentences.en: Wood was scheduled to be executed.
sentences.zh: 伍德被安排执行死刑。

sentences.en: Greg managed to get a stay back then, no small feat in Texas, but eventually another execution date got set.
sentences.zh: 格雷格当时设法争取到了暂缓执行，这在德克萨斯州绝非易事，但最终还是定下了另一个执行日期。

sentences.en: So now he's got exactly 87 days to stop it.
sentences.zh: 所以现在他只剩下整整87天来阻止这一切了。

sentences.en: If you asked Greg, he could rattle off a bunch of holes he sees in the case, including that story from George Hall about the jailhouse informants.
sentences.zh: 如果你问格雷格，他能如数家珍地列出他在这起案件中看到的漏洞，包括乔治·霍尔关于监狱线人的那套说辞。

sentences.en: But an even bigger issue, he tells me, has to do with DNA.
sentences.zh: 但他告诉我，一个更大的问题与DNA有关。

sentences.en: After he took the case, he asked the courts to allow the retesting of a few pieces of evidence with newer technology.
sentences.zh: 接手案件后，他请求法院允许用新技术对几件证据进行重新检测。

sentences.en: A piece of a victim's clothing turned up male DNA, and it was not
sentences.zh: 受害者的一件衣物上检测出了男性DNA，而那并不是

sentences.en: David Wood's DNA.
sentences.zh: 大卫·伍德的DNA。

sentences.en: Since then,
sentences.zh: 从那以后，

sentences.en: Greg has been on a mission to get more evidence tested.
sentences.zh: 格雷格一直致力于推动更多证据的检测。

sentences.en: There are more than a hundred other pieces of evidence.
sentences.zh: 还有一百多件其他证据。

sentences.en: But the state of Texas has repeatedly said no.
sentences.zh: 但德克萨斯州一再拒绝。

sentences.en: So that's what Greg is focused on today.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是格雷格今天关注的重点。

sentences.en: His plan is to meet with James Montoya, the incoming DA, and convince him to support more DNA testing.
sentences.zh: 他的计划是会见候任地方检察官詹姆斯·蒙托亚，说服他支持进行更多的DNA检测。

sentences.en: And that's not all.
sentences.zh: 而且还不止这些。

sentences.en: There's this other thing.
sentences.zh: 还有另一件事。

sentences.en: I won't bore you with the details of why this happened, but just know that years ago, the El Paso DA handed this whole case off to the Texas Attorney General,
sentences.zh: 我就不细说这件事发生的原因了，但你要知道，几年前，埃尔帕索地方检察官把整个案子移交给了德克萨斯州总检察长，

sentences.en: a very pro-death penalty Republican.
sentences.zh: 那是一位非常支持死刑的共和党人。

sentences.en: So what Greg really wants is for Montoya, a Democrat, to ask for the case back, then ask the courts to halt the execution, and then test the DNA.
sentences.zh: 所以格雷格真正想要的是，让身为民主党人的蒙托亚把案子要回来，然后请求法院停止执行死刑，接着进行DNA检测。

sentences.en: Three huge asks.
sentences.zh: 三个巨大的诉求。

sentences.en: That's Greg's plan.
sentences.zh: 这就是格雷格的计划。

sentences.en: But maybe it's not accurate to call this a plan.
sentences.zh: 但或许称之为计划并不准确。

sentences.en: There's no meeting scheduled.
sentences.zh: 目前还没有安排会面。

sentences.en: In fact, it sounds like Montoya might not even know who Greg is.
sentences.zh: 事实上，听起来蒙托亚可能根本不知道格雷格是谁。

sentences.en: I left him the longest text message
sentences.zh: 我给他发了有史以来最长的短信，

sentences.en: I've ever sent to anyone about David Wood's case, asking for an opportunity to speak with him while I was in El Paso.
sentences.zh: 内容是关于大卫·伍德案的，请求在我身处埃尔帕索期间能有机会与他交谈。

sentences.en: Didn't hear back from him.
sentences.zh: 没收到他的回复。

sentences.en: That was about two weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 那大约是两周前的事了。

sentences.en: I left him a voicemail message this morning.
sentences.zh: 今天早上我给他留了语音留言。

sentences.en: Told him I'm in El Paso.
sentences.zh: 告诉他我人在埃尔帕索。

sentences.en: I flew in from
sentences.zh: 我是从

sentences.en: Madison, Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州麦迪逊市飞过来的。

sentences.en: Gonna be here for a few days.
sentences.zh: 会在这里待几天。

sentences.en: And I hope that he will speak with me for just a few minutes about David Wood's case.
sentences.zh: 我希望他能抽出几分钟时间，和我谈谈大卫·伍德的案子。

sentences.en: The DA's office is on the second floor of the courthouse, so we take the elevator up to a waiting area.
sentences.zh: 地方检察官办公室在法院二楼，所以我们乘电梯到了等候区。

sentences.en: There's a flat-screen TV playing the show Cake Wars.
sentences.zh: 那里有一台平板电视正在播放《蛋糕大战》节目。

sentences.en: Greg announces himself to a receptionist, and we sit.
sentences.zh: 格雷格向接待员通报了自己的身份，然后我们坐了下来。

sentences.en: Greg has invited us here, but he's not completely sold yet on being followed around with microphones.
sentences.zh: 格雷格邀请我们来这里，但他还没完全下定决心接受我们带着麦克风全程跟踪。

sentences.en: Or maybe not sold enough to let us tape him ambushing the next district attorney of El Paso.
sentences.zh: 或者说，还没下定决心让我们录下他伏击埃尔帕索下一任地方检察官的过程。

sentences.en: So, I'm just gonna tell you what happens next.
sentences.zh: 所以，我直接告诉你接下来发生了什么。

sentences.en: We wait for about ten minutes, and then a figure sweeps by, a sort of boyish young man in a suit, trailed by an aide.
sentences.zh: 我们等了大约十分钟，然后一个身影匆匆走过，那是一个穿着西装、看起来有些孩子气的年轻人，身后跟着一名助手。

sentences.en: And Greg leaps from his chair, and I realize, this is Montoya.
sentences.zh: 格雷格从椅子上一跃而起，我意识到，这就是蒙托亚。

sentences.en: The mood turns cringy very faSt.
sentences.zh: 气氛很快变得尴尬起来。

sentences.zh: 格雷格说，我们不能就谈五分钟吗？

sentences.en: Montoya says he has another meeting.
sentences.zh: 蒙托亚说他还有另一个会议。

sentences.en: Greg says, he came all the way from Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 格雷格说，他可是从威斯康星州远道而来的。

sentences.en: And Montoya gets blunt, says,
sentences.zh: 蒙托亚直截了当地说：

sentences.en: I'm telling you, it's not happening.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你，这事儿没戏。

sentences.en: So Greg changes tack, talking faster now, diving right for the bullet points.
sentences.zh: 于是格雷格改变了策略，说话速度加快，直接切入重点。

sentences.en: There's DNA from someone else.
sentences.zh: 有别人的DNA。

sentences.en: The execution date is just a few months away.
sentences.zh: 执行日期只剩几个月了。

sentences.en: They're talking over each other now, like they're performing monologues from two different plays.
sentences.zh: 他们现在各说各的，就像在表演两部不同剧目的独白。

sentences.en: I'm staring at my hands, fiddling with my wedding ring, and I look over at my producer Alvin, and he's doing the exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 我盯着自己的手，摆弄着结婚戒指，看向我的制片人阿尔文，他也在做着一模一样的动作。

sentences.en: Greg asks if he can come back in a few weeks.
sentences.zh: 格雷格问他几周后再来行不行。

sentences.en: And Montoya says, sure, but his answer will still be no.
sentences.zh: 蒙托亚说，可以，但他的回答依然会是拒绝。

sentences.en: Greg says, he'll come back anyway.
sentences.zh: 格雷格说，他还是会再来的。

sentences.en: This all takes less than two minutes, but it's like the awkwardness ripped a hole in the space-time continuum.
sentences.zh: 这一切发生的时间不到两分钟，但那种尴尬感仿佛撕裂了时空连续体。

sentences.en: It might as well have been a week.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像过了一周那么久。

sentences.en: We take the elevator back down, go outside, and turn the recorder back on for a debrief.
sentences.zh: 我们乘电梯回到楼下，走到外面，重新打开录音机进行复盘。

sentences.en: That was
sentences.zh: 那真是

sentences.en: very discouraging, very disappointing.
sentences.zh: 非常令人沮丧，非常令人失望。

sentences.en: I had higher hopes that he would be willing to get involved.
sentences.zh: 我曾抱有更高的期望，希望他愿意介入。

sentences.en: I wish he could give me
sentences.zh: 我真希望他能给我

sentences.en: 10 or 15 minutes and that I could go through the case in a very calm and logical manner.
sentences.zh: 10到15分钟，让我能以非常冷静和合乎逻辑的方式梳理一下案情。

sentences.en: I mean, I do understand he's taking over an office that's been in a lot of chaos over the last few years and they also have a huge case coming up,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我确实理解他接手的是一个过去几年一直处于混乱状态的办公室，而且他们还有一个巨大的案子要处理，

sentences.zh: 可能是自大卫·伍德案以来最大的案子，这就是

sentences.zh: 造成23人死亡的沃尔玛枪击案。

sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，也许这位新当选的

sentences.zh: 地方检察官已经够忙了，不想去搅和埃尔帕索最臭名昭著的连环杀手那场期待已久的死刑执行。

sentences.zh: 但格雷格只剩下

sentences.zh: 87天的时间来想办法让蒙托亚站在他这一边了。

sentences.zh: 我问他，考虑到刚才那次互动的过程，他是否对蒙托亚会和他交谈抱有任何现实的希望。

sentences.zh: 我是一个乐观主义者。

sentences.zh: 我不是那种天真的乐观主义者，但我确实心存希望，希望这次当我跑去踢球时，露西不会把球挪开。

sentences.zh: 查理·布朗是我的英雄。

sentences.zh: 查理·布朗，无论发生什么都坚持不懈。

sentences.zh: 格雷格告诉阿尔文和我，他认为在这样的死囚案件中，这种做法蕴含着智慧。

sentences.zh: 第二天早上，

sentences.zh: 阿尔文和我在机场附近一家非常米色的酒店大堂见到了格雷格。

sentences.en: Joining us is another lawyer who got in last night,
sentences.zh: 和我们一起的还有昨晚刚到的另一位律师，

sentences.zh: 杰里米·谢珀斯。

sentences.zh: 格雷格，你好吗？

sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.zh: 你感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: My knee feels like fucking shit from running the marathon, but other than that, not to...
sentences.zh: 跑完马拉松后我的膝盖感觉糟透了，但除此之外，不至于……

sentences.zh: 你跑了马拉松？

sentences.zh: 是啊，我跑了

sentences.zh: 杰里米本质上是

sentences.en: Greg thinks if there are news stories about the problems in David Wood's case, maybe that will push
sentences.zh: 格雷格认为，如果能有关于大卫·伍德案中存在问题的报道，也许能推动
